reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC2866-3-2.note: TestRFC2866SentAccountingRequestCarriesTheSection3Authenticator reads the Accounting-Request datagram SendToServers put on the wire and asserts its 16 authenticator octets equal an independent MD5(Code+ID+Length+16 zeros+attributes+secret) over that datagram, and differ from the random authenticator in the Packet. Exact equality over the sent octets fails on any formula or ordering deviation in client.go. The tampering negative stays helper-level (shows secret, attribute and Code feed the hash); the wire positive is what discriminates.

RFC2866-3-3.note: Clause 1: TestRFC2866AccountingRetransmitWithoutDelayTimeKeepsIdentifier goes red on a changed Identifier for identical contents. Clause 2: TestRFC2866AccountingRetransmitTakesANewIdentifierAndRequestAuthenticator forces a retransmit whose Acct-Delay-Time moves 0->1 and asserts a new Identifier, a new Request Authenticator, and each authenticator equal to the Section 3 MD5 of its own datagram. The two clauses are opposite polarities of one rule, so a client that always or never changes the ID goes red. TestRFC2866AccountingDistinctRequestsDifferIdentifier is mislabeled: it proves RFC2866-4.1-4.

RFC2866-3-5.note: Forbidden behaviour: accepting a datagram shorter than its Length field. TestRFC2866ShortPacketSilentlyDiscarded overstates the Length by 8 and fails if the exchange completes; TestRFC2866HonestLengthIsAccepted shows the same server with an honest Length completes, isolating the length claim.

RFC2866-4.1-1.note: Judge 2026-09-30 (cont 5). Clause 1 (the attribute holds the user's address): TestAcctFramedIPAddressPresent, TestAcctFramedIPAddressIsSubscriberNotNAS, the unset/IPv6 negative and test/l2tp/radius-acct-wire.ci, unchanged. Clause 2, the gap of the prior weak verdict, is now proven and was a real defect: extractAuthMetadata took Framed-IP-Address 255.255.255.254 as a unicast address, the pool pinned it and accounting reported it. Fix (extract.go framedIPNASSelects) leaves FramedIP unset for 0xFFFFFFFE, and 0xFFFFFFFF stays refused by isValidSubscriberIP (limited broadcast), so the pool assigns; RFC 2865 Section 5.8 text checked; 0.0.0.0 is refused as unspecified. Positive TestRFC2866AccountingReportsTheAddressTheNASAssigned: both special values with a Framed-Pool keep the pool and leave FramedIP unset, and Start/Interim/Stop each carry exactly one Framed-IP-Address equal to the assigned 100.64.0.9. Negative TestRFC2866SpecialFramedIPValueIsNeverTheSubscriberAddress: neither value, alone or beside Session-Timeout, becomes the subscriber address. Both recorded red on extractAuthMetadata. The pool step between extraction and the accounting session (session-ip-assigned) is not driven by these units; the .ci covers IPCP-to-accounting end to end. Note: 0xFFFFFFFF ('the NAS Should allow the user to select') is handled as NAS-selects, journaled in plan/journal/field-carries-two-meanings.md; not this row's clause.

RFC2866-4.1-2.note: Forbidden behaviour: User-Password, CHAP-Password, Reply-Message or State in an Accounting-Request. TestRFC2866AcctForbiddenAttributesAbsent checks each of the four (and CHAP-Challenge) on Start, Interim-Update and Stop from buildAcctPacket; the negative shows the packet still carries User-Name, Acct-Session-Id and Acct-Status-Type, so an empty builder cannot pass. The permissive first clause obliges the sender nothing.

RFC2866-4.1-3.note: Forbidden behaviour: an Accounting-Request carrying neither NAS-IP-Address nor NAS-Identifier. TestRFC2866AcctNASIdentityAlwaysPresent fails on that for every status and every leaf combination, including neither leaf set; TestRFC2866AcctNASIdentityFallbackIsNarrow shows the fallback does not replace a configured identity.

RFC2866-4.1-4.note: Triggers now isolated: the Acct-Delay-Time retransmit (no reply received, attributes changed) asserts a new Identifier; TestRFC2866IdentifierChangesAfterAValidReplyWithUnchangedAttributes sends two records with byte-identical attribute fields, the second after a valid reply, and asserts distinct Identifiers. The rule is one-directional (MUST change on either trigger), so the two positives carry it; the NextID counter negative is a counter property, not a violating input.

RFC2866-5-1.note: Judge 2026-09-30 (cont 6). Row corrected under R5 to the Section 5.13 legend line '1 Exactly one instance of this attribute MUST be present.' (verbatim), binding Acct-Status-Type and Acct-Session-Id; id kept because internal/le/rfc/quote_backfill_test.go pins it and the HEAD tags stay valid, which is honest: the id names the obligation the old span carried, narrowed. Positives: TestRFC2866AcctStatusTypePresent (count 1, right value, per status) and TestRFC2866EveryRecordCarriesOneOfEachOneMarkedAttribute (Start/Interim/Stop encoded and decoded: exactly one non-empty Acct-Status-Type and Acct-Session-Id, same session id). Negative TestRFC2866ExclusionsCannotRemoveAOneMarkedAttribute is genuine: the operator's attributes-exclude control is the only input that could drop either attribute; it refuses both names, and excluding every accepted name (derived from excludableAttributes) still leaves each exactly once. Recorded red on buildAcctPacket and parseAttributeExclusions. TestRFC2866AcctStatusTypeNeverOmitted still repeats the positive's presence check; the pair no longer depends on it.

RFC2866-5-2.note: Forbidden behaviour: a null octet read as a terminator. TestRFC2866EmbeddedNullsSurviveTheWire round-trips a value with interior nulls through EncodeTo and Decode and compares bytes; TestRFC2866AllNullValueKeepsItsLength fails if an all-null value loses length. A strcpy-style cut goes red in both.

RFC2866-5-3.note: Forbidden behaviour: a text attribute of length zero on the wire. TestRFC2866AcctZeroLengthTextOmitted builds all three records for a session with no username and fails on a User-Name or any zero-length attribute; TestRFC2866AcctNonEmptyTextIsSent shows a non-empty User-Name is still sent.

RFC2866-5.13-1.note: Judge 2026-09-30 (cont 7 re-judge). Row '0 This attribute MUST NOT be present' (Section 5.13 legend; User-Password, CHAP-Password, Reply-Message, State, CHAP-Challenge). Positive TestRFC2866LoggedInSessionAccountsWithoutZeroMarkedAttributes runs the real path: provider configured over plugin RPC, CHAP login through l2tp.GetAuthHandler against a live UDP server, session up/down over the event bus; the server decodes Start and Stop, which name the user and an Acct-Session-Id and carry none of the five. Negative TestRFC2866LoginCredentialsAndAcceptStateNeverReachAccounting is the missing piece of the prior weak verdict (R1(b), inputs forced toward the violation over the real path): a CHAP and a PAP login against an Access-Accept carrying State and Reply-Message; the test first proves CHAP-Challenge, a 17-octet CHAP-Password and User-Password were on the Access-Request wire, then that no Start/Stop of either session carries a 0-marked type or any of those octets (State, Reply-Message, challenge, CHAP response, CHAP-Password, PAP plaintext, hidden User-Password). Producer acct.go buildAcctPacket / acctSession holds only username, calling-station, NAS-Port-Id, peer address, so a copy would be a new input path, which the negative catches on the wire. Both new units observed red under a revert of buildAcctPacket. The builder-level pair in rfc2866_attribute_table_test.go keeps its HEAD tags; its negative (TLV framing) is supplementary.

RFC2866-5.5-1.note: Forbidden behaviour: two sessions whose records carry the same Acct-Session-Id in the log. TestRFC2866AcctSessionIDUnique (1600 concurrent ids) and TestRFC2866AcctSessionIDNoCollisionOnReusedKey prove uniqueness within one process lifetime. genSessionID (authradius/acct.go) is tunnel-session-counter with a counter that restarts at 1 on every start, and no tagged unit covers a restart; the RFC's own example reserves digits for the reboot count because the log outlives a reboot.
